top_choice_rationale: P001 (Kiyotaki and Moore, B006) rewards one well-bounded mechanism: borrowing limits tied to collateral values feed back on asset prices and activity, so small shocks become large, persistent credit cycles. The idea is about thirty years old and has shaped macro-finance and policy modelling. It was tested by 2007-09 and extended afterwards. The two-name attribution is the cleanest on the slate, since round 2 left no dispute over the originators and no one could name a clean separable Gertler claim. A citation limited to collateral and balance-sheet amplification avoids re-crediting the Bernanke-Gertler accelerator and the bank-run themes of the 2022 prize. The main reservations are that direct identification of the specific collateral channel is mixed and that the 2022 prize is adjacent. I treat both as reasons to word the citation narrowly, not as disqualifying. P002 (Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes) is a close second, with a compact, traceable core and a long applied record. Its cost is the omission of Bresnahan and Reiss under the three-name cap, and its counterfactuals depend on functional-form assumptions. P003 (Autor, Dorn and Hanson) has sound, repeatedly re-examined designs. I rank it third because of the technology/trade bundling and boundary questions, and because of overlap with the 2021, 2023 and 2024 prizes. All three proposals clear the bar for a prize, so I rank no award last. This rests on general background knowledge and not on independently verified citation or usage data.
recusal_note: Profile-based connections, disclosed and not adjudicated. I chair the committee and am a round-2 supporter of P001. I am an IIES colleague of Krusell and Boppart and have co-authored with Krusell, Boppart and Friberg. Krusell and Friberg also support P001, and Boppart supports P003. My profile documents no co-authorship or institutional tie to Kiyotaki, Moore, Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes, Autor, Dorn or Hanson. My macroeconomics field is adjacent to B006, and I have tried to apply the same criteria to every field.
